stance.label: Strong bounce within a US pullback; stay on plan

headline: SOX jumps 4.7%, TSMC ADR up 3.2%; US stocks rally on Black Friday, S&P 500 nears its 200-day line
summary: This was a strong bounce inside a US pullback: chips led and China's market support lit the spark, but volume was thin and Nvidia barely rose. The S&P 500 is still 0.8% below its 200-day line, so the rules still read pullback. Taiwan opens Monday with an ADR premium behind it; the key is whether foreigners end their 10-day selling streak.

watch.note: Closed 7,297.49 on 11/27, still 0.8% below; the line is rising, and a close back above ends the break

watch.label: QQQ tier 4 (−20% from high)

overview.lead: US stocks bounced hard after Thanksgiving, led by chips, but it was a thin half-day session and not enough to change the pullback call.
points: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% to 7,297.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.31% and the Dow gained 592 points.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 4.69%, the strongest corner of the market.
Nvidia (NVDA) rose only 0.8% and spent most of the session in the red.
US trading ended at 13:00 ET; thin volume can exaggerate moves.

focus.lead: Among the nine tracked names, the two US ETFs bounced and QQQ gained most; QQQ is still the closest to a tier, but the gap widened to 6.6%.
points: QQQ rose 2.69% and SPY 1.62%, data as of 11/27.
0050 stays at its 11/27 close of 92.40 and reflects the US session on Monday.
Fidelity Japan Value (LU0997587083) NAV rose 1.86% on 11/27.
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) and AB American Growth (LU0683600562) NAVs are only as of 11/25 and miss the chip rally.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) share 6 top-ten names, about 27% by weight.

position.lead: No new trigger under the framework today; the US bounce moved every name further from its next tier.
points: QQQ has used 45% of its reserve; tier 4 is 6.6% away.
SPY has used 25% of its reserve; tier 3 is 9.1% away.
0050 has used 70% of its reserve; tier 5 is 11.7% away.
AB American Growth tier 3 is 8.0% away (11/25 NAV).
Neuberger Berman Taiwan-Japan (TW000T5011A9) tier 5 is 11.0% away (11/26 NAV).
Fidelity Japan Value tier 5 is 12.3% away (11/27 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology, Cathay Taiwan High Dividend and AB International Technology have used all tiers.

macro.lead: Stocks recovered but bonds did not relax; rate-hike expectations remain, while credit markets stay calm.
points: The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.94%, up from 4.85% on 11/25.
The 20+ year Treasury ETF (TLT) fell 1.18% as money moved from safety back into stocks.
High-yield spreads are 3.77% (11/26), far from the 5% warning line.
USD/TWD is 33.189 (11/26); the Taiwan dollar is weak but not plunging.

sentiment.lead: Fear is easing but still in extreme fear, where bounces often chop back and forth.
points: The VIX fell to 23.81, down about 3 points in a day.
The CNN Fear & Greed Index is 24.9, up from 18.6 a week ago.
The VIX term structure is still flat; short-dated vol is not below longer-dated.
7 of 11 sectors are above their 200-day lines; breadth has not collapsed.

sectors.lead: The groups cut hardest earlier in the week bounced; tech and chips led while defensives lagged.
points: The semiconductor ETF (SMH) rose 4.17% and AMD (AMD) 4.56%.
Tech rose 2.8% and software 2.64%.
Tesla (TSLA) rose 5.22% and Amazon (AMZN) 3.96%.
Health care and utilities rose only 0.28%; money rotated back to offense.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan opens Monday with tailwinds from the SOX surge and a wider TSMC ADR premium, but foreign flows decide whether the bounce lasts.
points: The TSMC ADR (TSM) rose 3.21%, an implied premium of 7.6%.
Foreigners sold NT$29.6B on 11/27, a 10th straight day.
Foreign net TAIEX futures short is 107,503 contracts, a record for a third day.
TAIEX night futures were down 289 points around Taipei midnight, before US stocks hit their highs.
TWD is 33.189 (11/26); if foreigners stop selling, the currency should stop weakening first.

watch.lead: Next week's test is data: the 12/4 payrolls report sets rate-hike odds, and Taiwan watches when foreigners stop selling.
points: 11/30 Taiwan opens; see if TSMC prices in the ADR premium.
12/1 Jensen Huang faces a closed-door US House committee interview.
12/4 US November nonfarm payrolls (Taipei 21:30).
12/10 early morning FOMC decision; November CPI that evening.

regime.lead: By the rules, the US is still a pullback, not a turn down; Taiwan is still a bear market with rising risk.
points: Trend: the S&P 500 is 0.8% below its 200-day line, which is still rising; a bit more gain puts it back above.
Systemic lights: only 1 is on in the US, the index below its 200-day line.
Credit, the economy and financial conditions show no trouble; high-yield spreads are 3.77%, far from 5%.
Capitulation signals: 2 are on, an inverted vol curve and extreme fear; oversold and VIX panic are off.
US drops to this level usually stop at a correction: since 1929, only 19 of 169 went past −20%.
Of the 116 drops as fast as this one, only 8 went past −20%.
What flips it: 5 closes below the 200-day line at 7,354 with the line going flat means weak.
Only a break of 6,255 is a bear market; 3+ systemic lights on means it may be turning bearish.

news.title: US stocks close higher across the board in the early Black Friday close; Dow up 592, S&P 500 up 1.6%
news.read: The index is back near its 200-day line and the rules still read pullback; volume was thin, so discount the gain.

news.title: Chip stocks hit earlier in the week rebound about 4.7%; Nvidia red most of the day, ends up 0.8%
news.read: The chip bounce matters most for TSMC, 0050 and the two Taiwan funds; Nvidia lagging means breadth still needs confirming.

news.title: Beijing pledges a bigger state-fund role; China's chip index jumps a record 17.6%
news.read: It lit up Asian chip sentiment and started the overnight SOX surge; no size was given for the support.

news.title: TSMC ADR up 2.4% intraday; TAIEX night futures down 289 points around midnight
news.read: The ADR closed up 3.21% with the premium widening to 7.6%, supportive for TSMC on Monday; weak night futures reflect pre-weekend hedging.

news.title: Foreigners sell NT$29.6B, a 10th straight day; net TAIEX futures short hits a record 107,503 contracts
news.read: Until foreigners cover shorts despite the US bounce, discount any Taiwan rally.

news.title: October core PCE rises 3.3% year on year, above forecasts; December hike odds about 98%
news.read: The 10-year yield rose to 4.94%, and hike pressure still weighs on richly valued stocks; next test is 12/4 payrolls.
